clue.text: Former Palestinian group's regularly dirty deed

parts.note: ex- means former, as in an ex-partner
the PLO is the Palestine Liberation Organization

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word dirty, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A former Palestinian group is accused of a dirty deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'dirty', giving IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or daring feat, a synonym for a deed.

clue.text: The language of Tolkien and King Henry

parts.note: Elvis Presley, the King of rock and roll
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A language shared by Tolkien and a king named Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King and Henry' look like one monarch, but are Elvis and a unit symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien invented tongues for his elves in The Lord of the Rings, such as Quenya and Sindarin.

clue.text: Panda, say, moves conspiratorially, less noisily

indicators.note: the letters move into a new arrangement
less signals that some letters are subtracted before rearranging

explanation.surface: A panda creeps conspiratorially and more quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of 'noisily' from 'conspiratorially' and rearrange the rest. A Panda car was a British police car, once painted blue and white.
explanation.definitionFit: A panda car is an example of a police vehicle on the beat; 'say' marks it as an instance.

clue.text: Fledgling duck, large parts sodden

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, so O

indicators.note: the word for large parts the other, splitting it apart from within

parts.note: sodden means wet

explanation.surface: A young duck, large and sodden in parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' wants to be a bird, matching 'Fledgling', but it is zero. 'parts' puts L inside WET.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl just leaving the nest is an example of a fledgling bird.

clue.text: Sailor man at home makes shelter for himself

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
Paul is a man's name
in means at home

explanation.surface: A sailor at home builds himself a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for himself' hints that the word once also meant a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a waterproof canvas sheet used as a cover or shelter.

clue.text: Mark paid revised price on time, saving euros

indicators.note: saving in the sense of keeping safe inside, so one piece holds the other
something revised has been reworked, so the letters of price are put in a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for euros

explanation.surface: A shopper is given a mark on a bill after paying a revised price on time with euros saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges PRICE to RECIP; T follows, and 'saving' puts E inside to give REC-E-IPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is the written acknowledgement that a sum has been paid, so a mark showing payment.

clue.text: What scouts do in playground these days

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a British public playground
CE is Common Era, the present era

explanation.surface: What scouts get up to in a modern playground.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is a British public park with playing fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Recce is short for reconnaissance, the scouting out of territory that military scouts carry out.

clue.text: Is this mounted due to pact being broken?

indicators.note: a pact that is broken falls apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Is a rebellion launched because a pact was broken?
explanation.walkthrough: 'being broken' rearranges DUE TO PACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden seizure of power is said to be staged or mounted, like an attack.

clue.text: One point impresses current dunce

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: impresses as in presses into, so the current symbol goes inside the point

parts.note: a dot is a point
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: One argument impresses a modern fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'modern', but it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow-witted or foolish person, a synonym.

clue.text: The detectorist leaves out notice for speculator

indicators.note: the synonym for notice is omitted from the phrase

parts.note: to detect is to notice

explanation.surface: A metal detectorist ignores a notice, hoping to strike lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves out' drops DETECT, leaving THE + ORIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speculates, building ideas or hypotheses rather than proven facts.

clue.text: Group of relatives returned key

indicators.note: the picked group of letters is then read backwards
a group of the letters inside the word relatives is picked out

explanation.surface: A group of relatives come back holding a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of' picks LATIV from inside 'relatives'; 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital and key are synonyms as adjectives: both mean essential or crucial.

clue.text: Like loner about to tackle cryptic clues [4]

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a memo heading

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone like a loner is about to tackle some cryptic clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' is the anagram signal; the [4] is read as a Roman numeral and joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse is a loner, so being reclusive is being like one, shunning company.

clue.text: Band's half-hearted gesture on departing

definitions.meaning: a range of radio frequencies used for long-distance broadcasting
a brief, perfunctory flap of the hand as one leaves

explanation.surface: A band's members give a half-hearted wave as they leave the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Short wave is a radio band, and a short wave is a curt farewell gesture.

clue.text: Put off deciding to drop mining

indicators.note: the word mining is dropped from the end of the longer synonym

parts.note: determining means deciding or settling
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company is put off deciding whether to stop its mining operations.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage or put them off from acting.

clue.text: In middle of lesson she's trim and cool, moving about

definitions.text: In middle of lesson she's trim and cool, moving about

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another, here inside the middle letters
the two central letters of the word lesson are taken
the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: she's is she is, the letters SHES

explanation.surface: A teacher in mid-lesson is trim and composed, walking around the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving about' jumbles SHE'S TRIM COOL into CHOOLMISTRE, which goes 'In' the SS at the middle of 'lesson'. The whole clue also describes a teacher at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmistress is a female teacher, pictured here pacing a classroom mid-lesson.

clue.text: Remove public hotline

parts.note: overt means open or public
split as hot plus line: H for hot, a row is a line

explanation.surface: An instruction to take down a public telephone hotline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hotline' splits as hot (H) and line (ROW).
explanation.definitionFit: To topple a ruler from power is to remove them by force.

clue.text: I do business with head office myself to find des res

parts.note: to deal is to trade or do business
me refers to the speaker, oneself

explanation.surface: An estate agent tells head office they will do business on a fine house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'des res' is estate-agent slang for a desirable residence; Ideal Home is a British magazine and exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate agent's 'des res' is a desirable residence, a perfect house to live in.

clue.text: Comic, original one touring island in Irish

indicators.note: the whole assembled piece goes inside the Irish word

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

indicators.note: touring as in going round, so this pair surrounds the island letter

parts.note: new means original or novel
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An original comedian tours an island in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts the island I inside NEW+I, making NIEWI. He was the straight man of Morecambe and Wise, a British TV comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a celebrated British comedian, half of the Morecambe and Wise double act.

clue.text: Priest almost cut short poem

indicators.note: almost the whole word, losing its final letter

parts.note: a cleric is a priest or clergyman
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A priest almost cut his poem short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CLERIC to CLERI.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-line comic verse about a person, invented by Edmund Clerihew Bentley.

clue.text: Where food is entering last, ie being processed

indicators.note: being processed as food is digested, so the letters are broken down and rearranged

explanation.surface: Food enters last, being processed, as in a digestive system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being processed' rearranges ENTERING LAST IE, a pun on digestion.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower bowel holds digested food as it passes through the body, a cryptic description of the organ.

clue.text: A golf international's in trouble for playing slowly

indicators.note: the three pieces go inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfing international is in trouble for playing too slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf' and 'playing slowly' suggest slow play on the course; it is a musical tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction for a slow, leisurely tempo of performance.

clue.text: Stunner pirouetted and struck a different pose

indicators.note: a pirouette is a full spin, so the word turns round

parts.note: a Taser is an electric stun gun

explanation.surface: A stunning beauty spun round and struck a new pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' looks like a beauty, but it is a stun gun; 'pirouetted' turns TASER round.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit is to sit again, as for a portrait, so taking up another posture.

clue.text: Authority comes out with circular letter

parts.note: says means utters or comes out with
O is the round letter

explanation.surface: An authority issues a circular letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular letter' looks like a mailshot; it is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their permission or authority to act.

clue.text: Where to dig up a nugget or sphere?

definitions.text: Where to dig up a nugget

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
a field is a sphere of activity or expertise

explanation.surface: A puzzled prospector asks where to dig: a nugget, or something round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link, but in heraldry it is gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospectors dig for nuggets of precious metal in a mining district rich in ore.

clue.text: Relish occasional bits of glum sitcom

indicators.note: every other letter of the two words is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in occasional bits of a gloomy sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto and relish are synonyms for keen enjoyment or zest.

clue.text: Pair abandon misleading affair

indicators.note: the pair is abandoned, dropped from the longer word

parts.note: fooling means deceiving or misleading
a pair in cricket is two ducks in a match, each a nought, so two Os

explanation.surface: A couple give up a deceptive love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: A pair in cricket is out for nought in both innings, so OO.
explanation.definitionFit: A fling is a brief romantic affair.

clue.text: What magicians said when they worked with ropes

indicators.note: worked as in kneaded or manipulated, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A magician speaks a cue while performing a trick with ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges THEY ROPES.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjurors traditionally exclaim this phrase at the moment a trick is revealed.

clue.text: Music in Glyndebourne's more than topping

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the phrase has the word inside it

explanation.surface: The music at Glyndebourne, the English country-house opera festival, is better than excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' is British slang for excellent; 'icing on the cake' is an extra beyond what is already good.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing on the cake is something added to what is already good, so more than topping.

clue.text: Doctor twice hides special list of big names

indicators.note: the doubled word conceals a letter between its halves
the word for the doctor is written two times

parts.note: Doctor Who, the time-travelling hero of the BBC series

explanation.surface: A doctor twice conceals a special list of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' puts S between the two WHOs.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference directory of notable people, giving brief biographies of the eminent.

clue.text: Artist's leg twisted — recovery's seriously neglected

indicators.note: a twisted leg is bent out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
something neglected is left out, so this part is omitted

parts.note: the word recovery, its 's being a link meaning is
very means seriously, as in very ill

explanation.surface: A twisted leg, its recovery neglected badly, needs an artist?
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns LEG to ELG; 'neglected' drops VERY from RECOVERY to leave RECO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan-born painter of Toledo, a famous sixteenth-century painter; the 's is the link 'is'.
